message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"3.56","text":"To those who thought that he was not good (as the Scriptures say), he said, “Which of you will a son ask for bread—surely he will not give him a stone instead? Or if he also asks for a fish, surely he will not give him a snake instead? Therefore, if you, though evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give good things to those who ask him and to those who do his will?” To those who asserted that he was in a temple, he said, “Do not swear by heaven, because it is God’s throne, nor by the earth, because it is the footstool of his feet.” To those who had asserted beforehand that God desires sacrifices, he said, “God wants mercy and not sacrifices, knowledge of him and not whole burnt offerings.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τίνα ὑμῶν αἰτήσει υἱὸς ἄρτον, μὴ λίθον ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ;","chosen":"Which of you will a son ask for bread—surely he will not give him a stone instead?","rationale":"Preserves the supplied construction, in which the son asks one of the hearers and μή marks a question expecting a negative answer."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς αἰτουμένοις αὐτὸν","chosen":"those who ask him","rationale":"The middle-form participle is rendered idiomatically as requesting something from him."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς δὲ αὐτὸν διαβεβαιουμένοις ἐν ναῷ εἶναι","chosen":"To those who asserted that he was in a temple","rationale":"διαβεβαιόομαι conveys confident assertion; the pronoun’s referent is left as the source presents it."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς δὲ προλαβοῦσιν ὅτι θυσιῶν ὀρέγεται ὁ θεός","chosen":"To those who had asserted beforehand that God desires sacrifices","rationale":"προλαμβάνω indicates taking or advancing a position beforehand; “asserted beforehand” fits the following ὅτι clause."},{"source_quote":"ἐπίγνωσιν αὐτοῦ","chosen":"knowledge of him","rationale":"The genitive is taken objectively, referring to knowledge of God; “recognition of him” is also lexically possible."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"μήτε τὴν γῆν, ὅτι ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ ἐστίν. τοῖς δὲ προλαβοῦσιν","issue":"The printed text does not close the quotation after ἐστίν before resuming the narrative with τοῖς δὲ. The syntactic boundary remains clear, so the English closes the quotation there.","proposed_reading":"μήτε τὴν γῆν, ὅτι ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ ἐστίν.“ τοῖς δὲ προλαβοῦσιν","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3.57","text":"To those who had been persuaded that he was evil (as the Scriptures say), he said, “Do not call me good, for the good is one.” And again, “Become good and compassionate like the Father in the heavens, who makes the sun rise upon the good and the evil and brings rain upon the righteous and the unrighteous.” To those who had been deceived into supposing that there are many gods (as the Scriptures say), he said, “Hear, Israel: the Lord your God, the Lord, is one.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"μή με λέγε ἀγαθόν· ὁ γὰρ ἀγαθὸς εἷς ἐστίν","chosen":"Do not call me good, for the good is one","rationale":"Retains the substantival ὁ ἀγαθός as “the good” rather than replacing it with a familiar canonical formulation."},{"source_quote":"γίνεσθε ἀγαθοὶ καὶ οἰκτίρμονες","chosen":"Become good and compassionate","rationale":"γίνεσθε denotes becoming, while οἰκτίρμονες emphasizes compassion or mercy."},{"source_quote":"φέρει τὸν ὑετὸν","chosen":"brings rain","rationale":"Preserves the verb φέρει rather than harmonizing the wording to a familiar parallel."},{"source_quote":"πολλοὺς θεοὺς ὑπονοεῖν","chosen":"supposing that there are many gods","rationale":"ὑπονοέω denotes supposing or imagining; English supplies “there are” to express the predicate construction naturally."},{"source_quote":"κύριος ὁ θεὸς ὑμῶν κύριος εἷς ἐστίν","chosen":"the Lord your God, the Lord, is one","rationale":"Preserves the repeated κύριος and the plural possessive ὑμῶν without assimilating the quotation to another Greek form."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"3.58","text":"All the same, Simon, recognizing that Peter was compelling him to use the Scriptures as Jesus had taught, did not want an examination of the discourse about God to take place, although Peter had changed the examination, as Simon himself had demanded, so that it would proceed by question and answer. Nevertheless, the inquiry continued for three days. As the fourth day began to dawn, Simon set out by night for Tyre in Phoenicia. Not many days later, some of those who had gone ahead came and told Peter, “Simon, performing great wonders in Tyre, has astounded many of the people there and, through many slanders, has caused you to be hated.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Πέτρος αὐτὸν συνάγει ταῖς γραφαῖς χρῆσθαι","chosen":"Peter was compelling him to use the Scriptures","rationale":"συνάγει can express constraint or compulsion in this construction; the alternative “bringing him to use” is weaker."},{"source_quote":"εἰς τὸν περὶ θεοῦ λόγον ἐξέτασιν γενέσθαι","chosen":"an examination of the discourse about God to take place","rationale":"λόγος may mean discourse, teaching, or argument; “discourse” preserves the broad sense without identifying it with a particular doctrine."},{"source_quote":"μεταθεμένου τοῦ Πέτρου","chosen":"although Peter had changed the examination","rationale":"The object of μετατίθημι is implicit and is supplied from ἐξέτασιν; the following phrase specifies the new question-and-answer format."},{"source_quote":"ἡ ζήτησις τριῶν ἐπεκράτησεν ἡμερῶν","chosen":"the inquiry continued for three days","rationale":"ἐπικρατέω literally suggests holding sway, but with a genitive of duration it indicates that the inquiry persisted throughout the period."},{"source_quote":"τινες τῶν προόδων","chosen":"some of those who had gone ahead","rationale":"The substantival expression denotes people preceding the main party; “advance party” or “forerunners” are viable alternatives."},{"source_quote":"σὲ πολλαῖς διαβολαῖς μισεῖσθαι ἐποίησεν","chosen":"through many slanders, has caused you to be hated","rationale":"The dative gives the means by which Simon caused hostility toward Peter."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὁμῶς ὁ Σίμων","issue":"The edition prints ὁμῶς, which can suggest “similarly” or “in the same way,” where the context favors the adversative sense commonly written ὅμως, “nevertheless.” “All the same” preserves an intelligible contextual force while disclosing the orthographic uncertainty.","proposed_reading":"ὅμως ὁ Σίμων","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3.59","text":"When Peter heard this, on the following night he had the crowd of hearers assemble. All the same, when they had assembled, he said, “Since, as I was setting out toward the nations that declare that there are many gods, to proclaim and teach that God is one, ‘who created heaven and earth’ and everything in them, so that by loving him they might be able to be saved, evil got there first and, by the law of pairing, sent Simon ahead, so that, if people cease declaring that there are many gods, they may condemn those called gods on earth but suppose that there are many gods in heaven, so that, having never honored the good of sole rule, they may perish completely after punishment. And what is most terrible, because the true word possesses incomparable strength, by getting there first with his slanders he persuades them not to accept it from me at all, lest the slanderer himself be exposed as a devil in reality and the true word, once shown forth, be able to be believed. I must therefore overtake him quickly, so that the slander, if allowed to persist, does not gain complete control of everyone.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῶν ἀκροατῶν τὸν ὄχλον συνελθεῖν ἐποίησεν","chosen":"he had the crowd of hearers assemble","rationale":"The causative construction ποιεῖν with the infinitive indicates that Peter caused or arranged for the gathering."},{"source_quote":"τὰ ἔθνη τὰ πολλοὺς θεοὺς λέγοντα","chosen":"the nations that declare that there are many gods","rationale":"λέγειν with πολλοὺς θεούς conveys asserting the existence of many gods, not merely pronouncing the phrase."},{"source_quote":"τῷ τῆς συζυγίας νόμῳ","chosen":"by the law of pairing","rationale":"συζυγία denotes conjunction, yoking, or pairing and here refers to the work’s paired-agent framework; “law of conjunction” is a viable alternative."},{"source_quote":"καταγνόντες τῶν ἐπὶ γῆς λεγομένων","chosen":"they may condemn those called gods on earth","rationale":"“Gods” is supplied from the immediately preceding predicate πολλοὺς θεοὺς λέγειν; “those spoken of on earth” would preserve the ellipsis more formally but obscure its contextual content."},{"source_quote":"τὸ τῆς μοναρχίας τιμήσαντες καλὸν","chosen":"having honored the good of sole rule","rationale":"μοναρχία denotes rule by one or sole sovereignty. The negative μηδέποτε is understood with the participle: they never honor this good."},{"source_quote":"αὐτὸ μηδὲ τὴν ἀρχὴν ἀναδέξασθαί μου","chosen":"not to accept it from me at all","rationale":"αὐτό refers most naturally to the true word, while μηδὲ τὴν ἀρχήν is idiomatic for “not at all”; “not to accept it from me even at the outset” remains possible."},{"source_quote":"ὁ διαβάλλων αὐτὸς τῷ ὄντι διάβολος","chosen":"the slanderer himself be exposed as a devil in reality","rationale":"Rendering διαβάλλων as “slanderer” and διάβολος as “devil” preserves the source’s wordplay."},{"source_quote":"αὐτὸν ἐπικαταλαβεῖν","chosen":"overtake him","rationale":"ἐπικαταλαμβάνω here means catching up with someone who has gone ahead."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὁμῶς συνελθοῦσιν ἔφη","issue":"The edition again prints ὁμῶς. It can be understood as “similarly,” but the discourse context permits the adversative force “all the same,” commonly written ὅμως. The difference is interpretive and does not prevent a defensible translation.","proposed_reading":"ὅμως συνελθοῦσιν ἔφη","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3.60","text":"“Since, then, it is necessary to appoint someone in my place, one who will fill my position, let us all pray to God with one resolve, so that he himself may make evident the best of those among us, in order that, seated upon the Messiah’s chair, he may administer his church devoutly. Who, then, will be appointed? For by God’s counsel that man is designated blessed whom his lord will appoint over the service of his fellow servants, to give them their provisions at their proper time. Without taking thought, he says in his heart, ‘My lord is delaying his coming,’ and begins to beat his fellow servants, eating and drinking with both prostitutes and drunkards. The lord of that servant will come at an hour that he does not expect and on a day that he does not know, and he will cut him in two and place his unbelieving part with the hypocrites.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"μιᾷ προαιρέσει","chosen":"with one resolve","rationale":"προαίρεσις denotes deliberate purpose or resolve; the phrase calls for united intention in prayer."},{"source_quote":"τῶν ὄντων ἐν ἡμῖν τὸν κρείττονα","chosen":"the best of those among us","rationale":"The comparative κρείττονα functions contextually as selection of the superior member from the whole group; “the better one among us” is more formally literal."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τῆς χριστοῦ καθέδρας","chosen":"upon the Messiah’s chair","rationale":"χριστός functions independently as a title and is rendered “Messiah”; καθέδρα is the authoritative seat or chair."},{"source_quote":"τὴν αὐτοῦ ἐκκλησίαν εὐσεβῶς οἰκονομῇ","chosen":"he may administer his church devoutly","rationale":"οἰκονομέω denotes managing or administering, while εὐσεβῶς describes conduct marked by reverence or devotion."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τῆς θεραπείας τῶν συνδούλων αὐτοῦ","chosen":"over the service of his fellow servants","rationale":"θεραπεία may denote service, attendance, or a body of household attendants. “Over the household of his fellow servants” is another possible contextual rendering."},{"source_quote":"Χρονίζει ὁ κύριός μου ἐλθεῖν","chosen":"My lord is delaying his coming","rationale":"χρονίζειν with an infinitive means taking a long time or delaying the action; lowercase “lord” preserves the servant-master imagery without deciding whether a divine referent is foregrounded."},{"source_quote":"διχοτομήσει αὐτόν","chosen":"he will cut him in two","rationale":"Preserves the literal and violent image of διχοτομέω rather than weakening it to “punish severely.”"},{"source_quote":"τὸ ἀπιστοῦν αὐτοῦ μέρος μετὰ τῶν ὑποκριτῶν θήσει","chosen":"place his unbelieving part with the hypocrites","rationale":"The unusual wording describes a part of him as unbelieving. The translation preserves this rather than replacing it with the more familiar but textually different idea of assigning someone a portion."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"μὴ ἐννοούμενον καὶ λέγοντα ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ Χρονίζει ὁ κύριός μου ἐλθεῖν καὶ ἄρξηται τύπτειν τοὺς συνδούλους αὐτοῦ, ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων μετά τε πορνῶν καὶ μεθυόντων","issue":"The construction shifts from accusative participles connected with ὃν to the finite subjunctive ἄρξηται and then to nominative participles. The scope of μή is also ambiguous: it may negate only “taking thought,” as reflected in the main rendering, or function as a warning against both saying that the lord delays and beginning the abuse. The sentence is anacoluthic, but every surviving clause permits a defensible contextual rendering.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
